answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource, like a bonded deposit, before it can transact, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real capital. Reputation then accrues slowly through attested work: a quartz-clear audit trail, jade-grade trust scores earned over time, and pearl-like credentials that cannot be copied or transferred. An attacker must pay the stake for every identity and wait out the slow reputation build, making mass fakery expensive and slow while honest agents operate cheaply.
